title: Cognitive Biases in Large Language Models: A Survey and Mitigation Experiments

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating pairs of responses twice with their presentation order swapped to check if the model consistently selects the same response or changes its preference based on position.
Comparing the model's evaluations when using actual model names versus anonymized placeholder names to test if it outputs consistent results regardless of anonymization.
Appending the identifier '(You)' to one of the response options in the prompt to test if the evaluating LLM preferentially selects the response attributed to itself.

Injecting statements into the prompt indicating that a majority percentage of people prefer a specific response, evaluating if the LLM changes its selection to conform to the simulated popular opinion.

Adding irrelevant distraction sentences (e.g., facts about eating apples or playing sports) to the instructions for one of the responses to see if the irrelevant information distorts the model's judgment.
Analyzing the model's selections based on the token count of the responses to measure the baseline percentage at which it favors longer responses regardless of quality.
